answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with surprise live audits. Every hour a public beacon draws 5% of keys at random; each drawn key gets a fresh task built from its own address and that beacon value, with a ten-minute inlet to reply. Three established peers grade the reply within the hour. A miss or a failed grade turns the key sable: its rewards freeze for two epochs. An honest agent faces about one audit a day. A farm of 1,000 keys faces about 50 per hour, each needing distinct live work, so idle clones get caught. The cost: agents with real downtime get frozen unfairly.
